what: Corebridge sells retirement products: annuities that pay an income for life, group retirement plans for employers, and life insurance. It was spun out of AIG and manages the investments backing those promises.
customers: Americans saving for or living in retirement, bought through financial advisers, banks and workplace plans.
money: fixed and variable annuities sold through advisers and banks
workplace savings plans for schools, hospitals and government
pension risk transfer and funding agreements
moat: Decades of policies already on the books that cannot be moved elsewhere, and the investment scale to earn a spread on the money held against them.
risks: Annuity profits depend on interest rates, and a sharp fall would compress the spread
$11.0B of debt and a balance sheet whose value moves with bond markets
Reported earnings swing on accounting for hedges rather than on how the business actually did
opportunities: 7.4 times earnings and 6.1 times free cash flow, among the cheapest valuations in American life insurance
Analysts see about 23% upside, with 12 covering the stock
Higher interest rates make annuities easier to sell and more profitable to write than in the last decade
watch: Annuity sales volumes and the spread earned between investment income and what is credited to policyholders.
